content: Children diagnosed with type 1 diabetes are at an increased risk of developing other autoimmune conditions, including thyroid dysfunction. It is recommended to test for thyroid antibodies, specifically antithyroid peroxidase and antithyroglobulin antibodies, at the time of diabetes diagnosis and periodically thereafter if the results are positive. Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels should be assessed at the time of diagnosis or shortly afterward, particularly if maintaining stable glucose levels proves challenging. If the initial TSH levels are normal, it is advised to recheck TSH every 1 to 2 years, especially if the child exhibits symptoms of thyroid dysfunction or has a positive family history of thyroid-related conditions. Thyroid dysfunction, such as hypothyroidism, can have significant effects on growth and metabolic control, necessitating careful monitoring and management.
